North China block underwent simultaneous true polar wander and
tectonic convergence in late Jurassic: New paleomagnetic constraints
∗
Yangjun Gao, Shihong Zhang , Hanqing Zhao, Qiang Ren, Tianshui Yang, Huaichun Wu,
Haiyan Li
State Key Laboratory of Biogeology and Environmental Geology, China University of Geosciences, Beijing, 100083, China
a r t i c l e i n f o a b s t r a c t
Article history: Jurassic witnessed two synchronous events on the Earth, named true polar wander (TPW) and closure
Received 6 January 2021 of the Mongol–Okhotsk ocean (MOO) between Siberia and eastern Asian blocks. The paleogeographic
Received in revised form 11 April 2021 change of the north China block (NCB) should thus include both TPW and plate tectonic components

Keywords: dp/dm=5.4 ◦ /7.1 ◦ (ca. 170 Ma). A positive untilting test indicates a pre-folding origin interpretation for
true polar wander the ca. 160 Ma pole. Quality of these poles is enforced by three positive conglomerate tests, the presence
Mongol–Okhotsk ocean of magnetic reversals and secular variation analyses. Comparison of the apparent polar wander paths
Middle and Late Jurassic of Eurasia and the NCB suggests that the NCB accreted to Eurasia around 140 Ma. The NCB and its
north China block then connected blocks did not undergo any significant southward paleogeographic shift during Jurassic.
paleomagnetism In context of TPW, we estimate a net northward plate moving velocity at 0.50–0.75 ◦ /myr for the NCB
in Jurassic. The long-term accumulation of MOO subducted slabs at the high paleolatitudes may have
critically contributed to, or perhaps led to, the Jurassic TPW.

In summary, three paleopoles newly obtained from the Juras-
(Besse and Courtillot, 2002; Kent and Irving, 2010; Torsvik et al.,
sic strata in the NCB meet all the seven criteria from the revised
2012; Yi et al., 2019). Based on different filtering methods applied
seven-point criterion system (Meert et al., 2020): R1, well-dated
to paleomagnetic data, two global apparent polar wander (GAPW)
strata; R2, proper techniques and statistical analyses including pos- paths have been proposed, which provide alternative views of the
itive PSV test; R3, evaluation of the remanence carriers; R4, posi- Jurassic TPW. Torsvik et al. (2012) used extensive paleomagnetic
tive conglomerate tests for the three poles and a positive untilt- datasets with quality factors Q ≥3 (Van der Voo, 1990), which in-
ing test for the ca. 160 Ma pole; R5, good structural control; R6, cluded volcanic and sedimentary poles after inclination shallowing
presence of magnetic reversals; and R7, no suspicion of remagneti- corrections. They then computed a GAPW path after applying a
